title: Enterprise social-media participation is broad but strongly stratified by firm size and country
source_unit: Eurostat 2025 EU survey on ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises, published 12 June 2026
geography: European Union; enterprises with 10 or more employees or self-employed persons in covered NACE sections

observations.period: 2025; enterprise social-media use by firm size

denominator.unit: EU enterprises with at least 10 employees or self-employed persons in covered NACE sectors; comparative percentage frame

social_media_any_total.unit: percent of covered EU enterprises using any type of social media

social_media_small_enterprises.unit: percent among small enterprises with 10-49 employees or self-employed persons

social_media_medium_enterprises.unit: percent among medium enterprises with 50-249 employees or self-employed persons

social_media_large_enterprises.unit: percent among large enterprises with 250 or more employees or self-employed persons

size_gradient.unit: percentage-point gap between large and small enterprise use

change_since_2023.unit: percentage-point increase in overall enterprise use from 61.1% in 2023 to 63.6% in 2025

mechanism.value: Social-media presence is becoming ordinary enterprise infrastructure, but smaller firms remain less able or willing to enter the same discovery, marketing, customer-contact, and collaboration layer as large firms

observations.method: Eurostat summary of the 2025 EU survey on ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises; social media includes use to increase online presence, marketing, communication, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing.
observations.uncertainty: Enterprise use is a broad binary indicator and does not measure audience reach, spending, conversion, platform dependence, content quality, labor burden, customer outcomes, or whether use is active, effective, or commercially important.
observations.subgroup: Small, medium, and large enterprises in covered NACE Rev. 2 sections and group 95.1.
observations.counterinterpretation: Large firms may have different sector mix, regulatory exposure, customer base, staffing, and brand needs; lower small-firm use does not prove exclusion from consumer discovery or lower business performance.

denominator.unit: covered enterprises in each EU country; comparative percentage frame

highest_country.unit: reported country shares of enterprises using social media

lowest_country.unit: reported country shares of enterprises using social media

country_range.unit: percentage-point difference between Malta and Bulgaria

mechanism.value: Enterprise access to consumer-facing digital discovery is geographically uneven, linking platform participation to connectivity, skills, firm structure, market composition, and national digitalization conditions

observations.method: Eurostat country comparison from the 2025 EU survey on ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises, restricted to the covered enterprise population.
observations.uncertainty: Country differences are descriptive and may combine infrastructure, sector composition, firm size, language, labor, marketing norms, and survey response effects; they do not identify which firms reach consumers or whether social-media use changes market power.
observations.subgroup: Covered enterprises across EU Member States.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low reported enterprise social-media use may reflect alternative channels, sector-specific business models, or lower need for public-facing promotion rather than digital exclusion or weak consumer access.

related_sources.claim: Eurostat methodological and data context for enterprise social-media use.
Eurostat digital-economy database route for the isoc_cismt source dataset.

boundary: This record adds a harmonized enterprise-side platform-discovery and digital-market participation layer. It does not establish consumer exposure, sales conversion, firm survival, labor effects, platform dependence, causal productivity, or cultural influence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Eurostat 12 June 2026 article retrieved; 2025 EU enterprise total, 2023 comparison, firm-size breakdown, country range, covered enterprise population, and stated purposes reviewed.
